question: What will the Arctic sea ice extent be on September 27, 2026, according to the NSIDC Sea Ice Index?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the daily Arctic sea ice extent for 2026-09-27 in the NSIDC Sea Ice Index version 4 daily file (N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), in millions of square kilometers.
research:
I couldn't find any pre-close event that settles this. In the NSIDC daily file, the last value likely published before close is **4.911 on 2026-08-29**, and ice was still falling fast.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 daily file, [N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv). Values are in million km².
- Late-August 2026 rows in that file:
  - 2026-08-16: 5.334
  - 2026-08-18: 5.414 (a brief rise)
  - 2026-08-20: 5.303
  - 2026-08-22: 5.117
  - 2026-08-24: 5.087
  - 2026-08-25: 4.998
  - 2026-08-26: 4.983
  - 2026-08-27: 5.028
  - 2026-08-28: 4.960
  - 2026-08-29: 4.911
- There is also a 2026-08-30 row showing 4.849. Daily values usually post with about a one-day lag, so it was probably not public before the 18:00 UTC close.
- I read the file as it stands now. Recent days can be revised slightly after first posting, so the numbers seen on Aug 30 may have differed by a few thousandths.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question. Extent fell about 0.5 million km² from Aug 18 to Aug 29, roughly 45,000 km² per day.
- In recent years the seasonal minimum has typically come between about Sep 10 and Sep 21. After that, extent usually rises by late September (see section 4).

## 3. Recent news (newest first, up to Aug 30 only)
- 2026-08-03: The Met Office said extent on Aug 2 was 7.02M km² (its dataset), 9th lowest for the date. July 2026 averaged 8.29M km², joint 5th lowest. The Kara Sea was exceptionally low. [Met Office Aug briefing](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- Summer 2026: a persistent low over the pole kept conditions cool and cloudy, which slowed melt. Melt onset in the Chukchi Sea was nearly a month late. This comes from an NSIDC analysis dated Sep 3, so I only mention it as context. [NSIDC](https://nsidc.org/sea-ice-today/analyses/arctic-zigs-antarctic-zags)
- I could not open the late-August Alaska climate Substack posts or the Arctic Sea Ice Forum page (both returned 403 errors).

## 4. Base rates (NSIDC daily file)
| Year | Aug 29 | Sep min (date) | Sep 27 | Sep 27 minus Aug 29 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2017 | 4.945 | 4.635 (Sep 13) | 5.080 | +0.135 |
| 2018 | 5.010 | 4.630 (Sep 21) | 4.884 | -0.126 |
| 2019 | 4.649 | 4.166 (Sep 18) | 4.563 | -0.086 |
| 2020 | 4.329 | 3.793 (Sep 13) | 4.272 | -0.057 |
| 2021 | 5.137 | 4.757 (Sep 14) | 5.171 | +0.034 |
| 2022 | 5.226 | 4.692 (Sep 15) | 5.079 | -0.147 |
| 2023 | 4.642 | 4.244 (Sep 17) | 4.463 | -0.179 |
| 2024 | 4.440 | 4.245 (Sep 10) | 4.544 | +0.104 |
| 2025 | 4.828 | 4.543 (Sep 8) | 4.919 | +0.091 |
- Sources: the [NSIDC daily CSV](https://noaadata.apps.nsidc.org/NOAA/G02135/north/daily/data/N_seaice_extent_daily_v4.0.csv), read in chunks; the 2025 minimum comes from its September 2025 rows.
- The change from Aug 29 to Sep 27 averaged about -0.03 over 2017-2025. It ranged from -0.18 to +0.14, with a standard deviation of about 0.12.
- Adding that change to 2026's 4.911 gives roughly 4.73 to 5.05, centred near 4.88. That is my arithmetic, not a forecast.
- From the minimum to Sep 27, extent rose between +0.03 and +0.48 in these years.
- Day-to-day noise in late September is about ±0.05 (for example, 2025-09-23: 4.845, Sep 24: 4.760, Sep 25: 4.817).
- 2026 entered late August with a steeper decline than most recent years.

## 5. Other forecasts
- The June 2026 Sea Ice Outlook had 18 entries for the September extent. The median was 4.83M km², with a range of 4.22 to 5.18. [Met Office July briefing](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic-and-antarctic-sea-ice-july-2026)
- 2026-08-03: The Met Office called the September minimum "very likely" within the post-2007 range of 3.99 to 5.68M km². Its statistical methods gave 3.98 to 5.45 and 4.05 to 5.39. [Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/approach/monitoring/sea-ice/2026/briefing-on-arctic--antarctic-sea-ice---august-2026)
- I could not find the July or August 2026 Sea Ice Outlook medians.
- Polymarket has markets on the 2026 minimum, defined as the lowest daily NSIDC value from Aug 1 to Oct 1. That is the minimum, not the Sep 27 value. I only saw aggregator prices with unclear dates, which conflict and are unreliable. A 2026-05-19 [Lines article](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/science/min-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer) put "No" on a minimum of 5M+ at 79%. Other listings: [orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/will-the-minimum-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer-be-between-4pt8m-5m-square-kilometers), [struct.to](https://explorer.struct.to/markets/will-the-minimum-arctic-sea-ice-extent-this-summer-be-at-least-5m-square-kilometers).
- I found no Kalshi or Manifold market on the Sep 27 value.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Early to mid September: the timing and depth of the seasonal minimum. Wind-driven compaction or spreading of the ice and late storms are the main swing factors.
- Early September: NSIDC's monthly analysis and the August Sea Ice Outlook.
- Mid to late September: NSIDC's preliminary minimum announcement, and the pace of refreeze in the Beaufort, Chukchi and East Siberian Seas, which were largely open water in late August.
- Around Sep 28: the Sep 27 value is posted. It can be revised slightly in the following days.
